summary: Four-row numeric list widget: four 0x14-byte row records (digit byte + 3-word screen position + pane id), a selection cursor object at +0x9C and a weighted-total display; embedded in the dialog/menu page windows that show a 4-digit entry (e.g. shop quantity/price style totals).
evidence: Ui_FourRowList_ScrollRow 0x003F7024 indexes the row array with self->f_49 * 0x14 and copies row +0x50/+0x54/+0x58 into the cursor node at +0x9C (+0x1C..+0x24); Ui_FourRowList_FormatRowValues 0x003F70D0 builds the total f_88*1000000 + f_74*100000 + digit*10000 + f_4c*1000 and clamps it at +0xA0; maybe_Ui_FourRowList_Reset ends with a vtable call through *self slot +0x18. Note: Ui_FourRowList_InitRowDefaults 0x003F6FAC initialises a separate 0x44-byte defaults record, so its +0x30/+0x40 stores are not certainly widget fields.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_FourRowList_Reset (0x003F71C0) dispatches (**(code**)(*self + 0x18))(self,1); ScrollRow/UpdateCursorGeometry also tail-call through the object's first word. Ui_FourRowList_InitRowDefaults zeroes offset 0 of the separate defaults record.

fields.name: textBankId
fields.evidence: Clear/FormatRowValues pack it as (u32)self->f_28 << 0x10 | paneIndex for the pane-text setter 0x001A6680, i.e. the high half of a text-layer/pane text address.

fields.name: maybe_rowDefaultWord
fields.evidence: Only seen in Ui_FourRowList_InitRowDefaults (`*(u32 *)(rowConfig+0xc) = uVar2` copied from a global defaults block); may belong to that defaults record rather than to the list widget.

fields.name: maybe_rowDefaultMode
fields.evidence: Ui_FourRowList_InitRowDefaults writes 8 at rowConfig[0x10]; same caveat as +0x30, this is the default-config record.

fields.name: activeRow
fields.evidence: ScrollRow reads *self->f_49 as the selected row, subtracts the delta, wraps to 3/0 and multiplies it by 0x14 to pick the row record; Reset clears it.

fields.name: row0Digit
fields.evidence: First row record digit: FormatRowValues uses (short)*(char*)(self+0x4c)*1000 in the total; Clear zeroes it. Row records have stride 0x14.

fields.name: row0PosX
fields.evidence: Row 0 position word copied by Reset/ScrollRow into cursorNode->f_1C (a 3-word position triple).

fields.name: row0PosY
fields.evidence: Second word of the row 0 position triple, copied to cursorNode->f_20 by Reset/ScrollRow.

fields.name: row0PosZ
fields.evidence: Third word of the row 0 position triple, copied to cursorNode->f_24 by Reset/ScrollRow.

fields.name: row1Digit
fields.evidence: Second row digit (row 0 + 0x14); FormatRowValues multiplies it by 0x186A0 (100000) and Clear/Reset zero it.

fields.name: row2Digit
fields.evidence: Third row digit (row 0 + 0x28); FormatRowValues multiplies it by 0x186A0-like decimal weights and Reset zeroes it.

fields.name: row3Digit
fields.evidence: Fourth row digit (row 0 + 0x3C); FormatRowValues multiplies it by 0x0F4240 (1000000) and Reset zeroes it.

fields.name: cursorNode
fields.evidence: Reset stores self[0x27] into local iVar2 and writes iVar2->f_1C/f_20/f_24 = the active row position; ScrollRow does the same through self->f_9C, so this is the cursor/selection display object.

fields.name: maxValue
fields.evidence: FormatRowValues compares the computed weighted total against *(u32*)(self+0xA0) and clamps the digit fields down, then sets +0xA4 = +0xA0.

fields.name: currentValue
fields.evidence: FormatRowValues stores the weighted digit total here (f_88*1000000 + f_74*100000 + f_60*10000 + f_4C*1000); Clear/Reset zero it.

summary: Icon grid model: owns a 0x2900+ byte object with 113 icon slots (0x58 bytes at +0x828), 28 per-slot priority bytes at +0x18A, one embedded Ui_Window, one Ui_AnimRef and a Ui_FaceIcon; it re-binds icons from the player's progress value and animates the grid open/closed.
evidence: maybe_Ui_IconList_UpdateState 0x002C7584 reads a work progress value (func_0066B004(work+0x24A98,0x32)), clears 0x71 per-slot visibility bytes at +0x58, calls Ui_IconList_RefreshIcons and drives the close/open animation; Ui_IconList_AreAllIdle 0x00641BA4 walks 113 icon slots at self+0x828 stride 0x58; Ui_IconList_BindIcon 0x002C6250 binds a model entry through self->f_160->f_11C. The batch size (0x1D4) is only the highest recovered field, the real object extends past +0x2880.

fields.name: maybe_iconListId
fields.evidence: RefreshIcons/UpdateState resolve func_002C6190(self->f_20) and use the result as the icon-list object for Ui_IconList_BindIcon; the field is a handle/id, not a pointer.

fields.name: maybe_ownerHandle
fields.evidence: UpdateState takes the 0x001FFFFF-tagged handle at +0x24, looks it up in the 0x007B80C0 object registry, compares the class against g_actorBaseClass and calls vt[0x40](obj,4).

fields.name: window
fields.evidence: UpdateState uses self->f_44 with Ui_Window helpers (Window_ReleaseLayoutSpans, Ui_Object_PlayAnimationPoor, f_3058/f_3330) and guards it against null.

fields.name: animRef
fields.evidence: UpdateState calls Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes(&self->f_48->f_148,1); BindIcon passes self->f_48 to Gfx_BindIndexedResourceSet.

fields.name: maybe_frameStart
fields.evidence: Ui_IconList_Tick copies g_0072AA0C->f_80 into self->f_50 (the shared frame/timer record); UpdateState also writes it from the same record.

fields.name: maybe_frameEnd
fields.evidence: Ui_IconList_Tick copies g_0072AA0C->f_84 into self->f_54 next to frameStart.

fields.name: maybe_selectedIndex
fields.evidence: UpdateState loads self->f_D0 into uVar7, bounds it against the row count (rowList->f_60) and indexes a 0x10-byte entry array, then shows entry uVar7.

fields.name: maybe_entryCount
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_IconList_ApplyChange tests `0 < *(int*)(self+0xE4)`; role beyond a positive count is not proven.

fields.name: maybe_entryStore
fields.evidence: UpdateState passes &self->f_E8 to func_00297F00 (a reset/clear helper) in the rebuild path; looks like an embedded container/state block.

fields.name: faceIcon
fields.evidence: UpdateState calls maybe_Ui_FaceIcon_SetOnOff(&self->f_134) and clears f_144 together with it.

fields.name: maybe_isFaceIconOn
fields.evidence: Set to 0 in the same block that switches the face icon off; no other reader in this batch.

fields.name: maybe_modelHost
fields.evidence: BindIcon uses self->f_160->f_11C as the model entry set (Model_FindEntryById) and reads ->f_1C from it; so +0x160 points at an object owning a model/resource table at +0x11C.

fields.name: maybe_isClosing
fields.evidence: UpdateState: when the list is being torn down and f_188 != 0 it plays the close animation via func_002C8A1C(self,0), commits, clears f_188 and returns.

fields.name: maybe_hasCachedValue
fields.evidence: UpdateState uses f_189 as the cached progress value (0 -> 0x0098967F sentinel) and sets it to 1 after the first no-change refresh, so it doubles as an initialised flag.

fields.name: subObjectHost
fields.evidence: UpdateState allocates a 0x30-byte object with Mem_AllocAligned_2, constructs it with Ui_SubObjectHost_Ctor(ptr,0x32) and stores it at self->f_1D0.

summary: Small child-window list object initialised by maybe_Ui_ChildWindowList_Init (called from Ui_ListWindow_InitDataObjects): stores the owner window at +0xC, an embedded zeroed sub-object at +0x10, a -1.0f default at +0x1C and four more zeroed list/count words.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ChildWindowList_Init 0x0043FFC8 installs vtable 0x007610B0 then 0x0076FE10, stores param_2 (owner) at self[3]=+0xC, calls func_002ACF08(self+4) to init the embedded +0x10 block, writes -1.0f (0xBF800000) at +0x1C and zeroes +0x20..+0x34. Only one function is known for the class, so every field beyond the owner is low confidence.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor writes 0x007610B0, then overwrites it with 0x0076FE10 at the end; both are literal vtables.

fields.name: maybe_listA
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor immediately before the embedded block initialised at +0x10; purpose not proven.

fields.name: maybe_listB
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor next to +0x4; purpose not proven.

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: Ctor stores its second argument (the calling list window) at self[3] = +0xC.

fields.name: maybe_defaultValue
fields.evidence: Ctor writes 0xBF800000 = -1.0f at self[7] = +0x1C; likely an unset scroll/selection sentinel.

fields.name: maybe_childBegin
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor only; the class name suggests a child-window list but no accessor proves a begin pointer.

fields.name: maybe_childEnd
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor only, adjacent to maybe_childBegin.

fields.name: maybe_childCapacity
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor only, third word of the suspected child vector.

fields.name: maybe_listHead
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor only; could be an intrusive-list head sentinel.

fields.name: maybe_listTail
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor only, next to maybe_listHead.

fields.name: maybe_listCount
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor only; last word of the 0x38-byte object.

summary: Shop item-list state/window object: the row-population method owns a vtable-driven item list (row offset +0xC, page index +0x4C, column-enable bytes +0x50..+0x53, row provider +0x54), while the 0x1E9xxx step handlers of the same generated class read a small step record (member id +2, item id +4, quantity +0x14) and return the next handler pair from 0x007295C0.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_PopulateRows 0x00364CC0 dispatches vt[+0x6C] on self to get the row provider, uses self[0x13] (page), self[0x14]/+0x51/+0x52/+0x53 as column enables and self[0x15] as the name provider; Ui_ShopItemList_HandleInput/MoveCursor/OpenList (0x001E9454/0x001E9ABC/0x001EA238) instead treat the same parameter as a small step record (*shop = 0x007295C0[1], shop[1]=0x007295C0[2], shop[3]=row offset, *(u16*)(shop+4)=item id, shop[5]=quantity). The batch merged two uses; +0x1B0 is 0x6C*4 from the vt[+0x6C] dispatch, not a field.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: PopulateRows calls (**(code**)(*self + 0x6C))(self) to obtain the row provider, so +0 is a vtable in the list-window use; the step handlers overwrite +0 with the next handler word from 0x007295C0.

fields.name: maybe_selectedItemId
fields.evidence: The step handlers read the selected item id as *(u16*)(shop+4) and pass it to Item_LookupRecord/Shop_SellItem; the same word is also shop[1], the second word of the returned handler pair, so the two uses conflict.

fields.name: rowOffset
fields.evidence: All step handlers store the current scroll/row byte offset here (`shop[3] = (entryBase + rowIndex*0xC) - firstVisible`) and pass it to maybe_Ui_ItemIcon_PlaceInLine.

fields.name: quantity
fields.evidence: shop[5] is the purchase quantity: BeginBuy passes it to Shop_SellItem, SelectQuantity reads it from the spin control at screen+0x1E51, and ConfirmEntry multiplies item price * shop[5].

fields.name: pageIndex
fields.evidence: PopulateRows uses self[0x13] as the first row of the page (self[0x13]*0xC row stride) and prints pageIndex+1 in the page counter.

fields.name: maybe_showOwnedColumn
fields.evidence: PopulateRows gates the owned/equipped marker column on `(char)self[0x14] != 0`; the field is word-sized in the decompiler but only the low byte is tested.

fields.name: maybe_showPriceColumn
fields.evidence: PopulateRows writes the price string only when *(char*)(self+0x51) is set.

fields.name: maybe_showStockColumn
fields.evidence: PopulateRows writes the stock/owned text only when *(char*)(self+0x52) is set.

fields.name: maybe_showPageCounter
fields.evidence: PopulateRows formats the page X/Y strings (panes 0x2A/0x2B) only when *(char*)(self+0x53) is set.

fields.name: rowProvider
fields.evidence: PopulateRows: piVar10 = self[0x15]; when null it falls back to *0x007AC270, otherwise it calls vt[+8](rowDesc, itemRecord) to obtain the item name; so +0x54 is the row/name provider object.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot6c
fields.evidence: Artifact: the only evidence is `(**(code**)(*param_1 + 0x6C))(param_1)`, a vtable dispatch at slot 0x6C. struct_db multiplied the slot by 4 and emitted offset 0x1B0; there is no object field there in the 0x1B4-byte row-list object.

summary: 0x50-byte animation-reference group used by many UI windows: an owner word at +0, a named pane group at +4 and an embedded Anim_AnimClip starting at +8 (the vtable 0x00769ED8 belongs to that sub-object), with default timing fields and a self-linked list sentinel.
evidence: Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor 0x003E0454 zeroes +0/+4, calls Anim_AnimClip_Ctor(self+2 words = +8) and installs vtable 0x00769ED8 on that sub-object; maybe_Ui_AnimRefList_Init 0x00473C18 stores the owner at +0 and self-links the clip lists; Ui_AnimRefList_BindNamedPanes 0x00473A9C stores the 'lastspurt' pane group from src->f_14 at +4 and binds the clip at +8.

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: Ui_AnimRefList_Init stores its owner argument at +0; the Ctor zeroes it. The vtable 0x00769ED8 is installed on the embedded Anim_AnimClip at +8, not at +0.

fields.name: paneGroup
fields.evidence: BindNamedPanes stores func_0053649C(src->f_14,"lastspurt") here and walks it to clear each child's +0x44 bit 0.

fields.name: maybe_clipField0
fields.evidence: Embedded Anim_AnimClip default timing word; the raw body stores 0 into clip+0xC (reported at +0x30 because struct_db treated the clip sub-object as base).

fields.name: maybe_clipField1
fields.evidence: Second zeroed clip timing word (clip+0xD) from Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor.

fields.name: maybe_clipField2
fields.evidence: Third zeroed clip timing word (clip+0xE) from Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor.

fields.name: maybe_clipField3
fields.evidence: Zeroed clip timing word (clip+0xF) from Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor.

fields.name: maybe_clipField4
fields.evidence: Zeroed clip timing word (clip+0x10) from Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor.

fields.name: maybe_clipSpeed
fields.evidence: Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor writes 0x3F800000 = 1.0f into the last clip default word (clip+0x11).

fields.name: maybe_nextGroupOffset
fields.evidence: Only evidence is Ui_AnimRefList_CreateTriple calling Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor on object+0x4C, i.e. the start of the next 0x50-byte group, not a field of this group.

summary: Base UI node registered in the global priority-sorted node list at 0x007A9B20: vtable 0x007655C4 at +0, an intrusive-list link triple at +4..+0xC, id/priority words and boolean state bytes, plus the pane text-bank id at +0x28. Every window root is inserted with Ui_NodeList_Register.
evidence: Ui_NodeList_Register 0x0036B45C installs 0x007655C4, self-links the three list words, stores priority (byte at +0x10), id (u16 at +0x12), zeroes +0x14/+0x16/+0x17/+0x18, sets +0x19/+0x1A to 1, and inserts the node at +4 into the global list by comparing *(+0x10). maybe_Ui_NodeList_CreateChildSlots 0x0036B5D4 uses +0x28 as the text-bank id for pane indices 0..8 and 10..18.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_NodeList_Register writes the literal 0x007655C4 at node+0; all dispatch goes through it.

fields.name: maybe_listNext
fields.evidence: Second word of the intrusive-link triple initialised by Ui_NodeList_Register (`node[2] = &node[1]`), which func_001235A4 links into the global node list.

fields.name: maybe_listPrev
fields.evidence: Third word of the same self-referential link triple (`node[3] = &node[1]`).

fields.name: nodeId
fields.evidence: Ui_NodeList_Register stores its third parameter (u16 id) at +0x12 and CreateChildSlots combines it with the text-bank id.

fields.name: maybe_flag16
fields.evidence: Explicitly zeroed by Ui_NodeList_Register; no reader in this batch, so only a boolean-state candidate.

fields.name: maybe_flag17
fields.evidence: Explicitly zeroed by Ui_NodeList_Register next to +0x16; no reader in this batch.

fields.name: maybe_isShown
fields.evidence: Set to 1 by Ui_NodeList_Register; register-time defaults for UI nodes are typically visible/enabled flags, but no consumer is in the evidence.

fields.name: maybe_isInteractive
fields.evidence: Set to 1 by Ui_NodeList_Register next to maybe_isShown; no reader in the evidence.

fields.name: textBankId
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_NodeList_CreateChildSlots passes paneId | self->f_28 << 0x10 to the pane-text setter 0x001A6680 for the 18 child panes.

summary: Field-UI gimmick object list (used by Field_Gimmick_SetupListFromConfig and the field UI-gimmick ctor/dtor): vtable at +0, a five-entry handle window at +4..+0x14, an append count at +0x84, ten embedded 0xC0-byte list slots at +0x88 and a second pair of slots at +0x254, plus a row/owner index byte at +0x808.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ObjectList_BuildEntries 0x005D19B8 appends up to five 0x220-byte draw objects, storing each handle at self+4+i*4 and using self->f_84 as the count; Ui_ObjectList_Clear 0x005D22E4 releases exactly f_84 handles from +4 and zeroes the count; Ui_ObjectList_InitSlotArray/ResetSlots 0x005D1978/0x005D27F0 release the ten 0xC0-byte slots at +0x88 and set f_808 to an owner/0xFF; the DestroySlots variants also release the two slots at +0x254. The class name is historical: the callers are field gimmick code, not a generic UI object list.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: The DestroySlots variants install 0x00783D04, 0x00783D14 and 0x00783D24 at +0 (each variant has its own table).

fields.name: entryHandle0
fields.evidence: First appended draw-object handle: BuildEntries stores a handle at self+4; ReleaseRefPairA/Clear release it with func_001C7570 and invalidate it to 0xFFFFF800.

fields.name: entryHandle1
fields.evidence: Second handle of the five-entry window; released by Ui_ObjectList_ReleaseRefPairA (self->f_C).

fields.name: entryHandle2
fields.evidence: Third handle; released by Ui_ObjectList_ReleaseRefPairB (self+8) and swapped by Ui_ObjectList_SwapOrder.

fields.name: entryHandle3
fields.evidence: Fourth handle (self->f_14); SwapOrder rotates it through +4/+8/+C/+10 when the player scrolls.

fields.name: entryCount
fields.evidence: BuildEntries increments self->f_84 after each appended object; Clear loops `i < self->f_84` and resets it to 0.

fields.name: slots
fields.evidence: Start of the ten embedded 0xC0-byte slots addressed as self + i*0xC0 + 0x88 by ClassifyEntryTypes, InitSlotArray and ResetSlots.

fields.name: maybe_slotsB
fields.evidence: Start of the two additional 0xC0-byte slots at +0x254 released by Ui_ObjectList_DestroySlotsA/Alt (`self + i*0xC0 + 0x254`, i < 2).

fields.name: maybe_ownerIndex
fields.evidence: InitSlotArray stores an owner at f_808, ResetSlots stores 0xFF and BuildEntries computes the row offset as f_808 mod 5, so it is a row/owner index byte.

summary: Large menu/page row-list widget (0x48BC bytes): an embedded animation controller at +0x11C, a Ui_RowList row block at +0xBC8, the selected row id at +0x724, an accept flag at +0x726, a per-row flag widget at +0x1928 and the packed input mask/axis bytes at +0x48B4..+0x48B8.
evidence: The three OnInput variants (0x0025C1DC, 0x0025E380, 0x0025E4EC) read the input mask at +0x48B4, dispatch vt[+0x14](animId)/vt[+0x10] on the object at +0x11C, look up the current row with Ui_RowData_AtIndex(&self->f_BC8) (0x0045D9F8: vtable at +0, 0xCC-byte rows from +0x14), store the row id at +0x724, set +0x726 and mirror row->f_321 into the object at +0x1928. The class is vtable-only (no direct caller), so the 'PaneList' label is not confirmed.

fields.name: maybe_animController
fields.evidence: Embedded object at +0x11C: code calls its vtable slots +0x10 (play pending) and +0x14 (play animation id, returns bool) for ids 0x2A/0x28/0x20/0x3B.

fields.name: selectedRowId
fields.evidence: All three OnInput variants store row->f_10 (the id of the row returned by Ui_RowData_AtIndex) at page->f_724.

fields.name: maybe_isInputAccepted
fields.evidence: Set to 1 on the accept mask 0x142 right after playing the accept animation.

fields.name: rowList
fields.evidence: Passed as &page->f_BC8 to Ui_RowData_AtIndex, whose body treats it as a row list (vtable at +0 and 0xCC-byte rows at +0x14).

fields.name: maybe_rowFlagWidget
fields.evidence: Every OnInput path ends with func_0029126C(&page->f_1928, row->f_321 != 0), a two-argument flag/visibility setter on the embedded object at +0x1928.

fields.name: inputMask
fields.evidence: The input handler tests it for the accept mask 0x142 and buttons 4, 8 and 1; the same word is consumed in all three variants.

fields.name: maybe_inputAxisX
fields.evidence: Forwarded sign-extended as the first of three key-vector arguments to the row list vt[+0x3C] when button 1 is pressed.

fields.name: maybe_inputAxisY
fields.evidence: Second sign-extended key-vector argument forwarded to the row list vt[+0x3C].

fields.name: maybe_inputAxisZ
fields.evidence: Third sign-extended key-vector argument forwarded to the row list vt[+0x3C].

summary: Present/item list container: vtable 0x00765D00 at +0, two circular intrusive-list sentinel pairs at +8/+0xC and +0x14/+0x18/+0x1C, a page row offset at +0x4C, the row provider at +0x50 and the entry source at +0x58; FormatItems fills nine visible rows and page counters.
evidence: Ui_PresentList_DeletingDtor/Dtor 0x0037BBBC/0x0037BC48 walk the element ring from self[6] until self[5], call element vt[+4], then re-link self[2]/[3] and self[6]/[7] sentinels; Ui_PresentList_FormatItems 0x0037C11C uses self[0x13] (page) * 9, the row source at self[0x16], the row provider at self[0x14] (f_58/f_60 row block) and the text-bank id at +0x28.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Both destructors install the literal 0x00765D00 at +0; vtable slots 0/1 are the dtor pair.

fields.name: maybe_listBegin
fields.evidence: First of the two sentinel words reset by the destructors (`iVar2 = self[2]; iVar4 = self[3]; prev/next re-link`).

fields.name: maybe_listEnd
fields.evidence: Second sentinel word reset by the destructors together with +8.

fields.name: maybe_listEndNode
fields.evidence: DeletingDtor loops `while (*piVar5 != self[5])` starting from self[6], so +0x14 is the ring terminator.

fields.name: maybe_listFirstNode
fields.evidence: Both destructors start the element walk at self[6] (+0x18).

fields.name: maybe_listLastNode
fields.evidence: self[7] (+0x1C) is re-linked with self[6] when the ring is reset.

fields.name: maybe_pageRowOffset
fields.evidence: FormatItems computes iVar6 = self[0x13] * 9 and then indexes rows iVar6..iVar6+8; it also prints page self[0x13]+1.

fields.name: rowProvider
fields.evidence: FormatItems reads self[0x14]->f_60 (row count) and self[0x14]->f_58->f_24 (0x0C-byte row records) to map a row index to an entry.

fields.name: maybe_entrySource
fields.evidence: self[0x16] is the object whose vt[+4](index) maps a global row index to an entry index and whose vt[+8](index) selects/plays that entry.

summary: Six-row skill/count list used by the skill panel: party member id at +0x49, up to six skill ids at +0x4A terminated by 0xFF, a text-bank id at +0x28, a row list pointer at +0x38, and four embedded Ui_AnimRef objects for the 3/4/5/6-row states at +0x50/+0xA0/+0xF0/+0x140.
evidence: Ui_SixRowCountList_SetEntries/Refresh 0x004533E8/0x00453520 read a party member id from +0x49 (checked < 0x1F, passed to func_0035EB98), copy the entry ids from the argument into a 0xFF-terminated byte array at +0x4A, count learned skills with Party_CountLearnedSkills/SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill and reset the anim ref chosen by the row count (self+0x14/0x28/0x3C/0x50 words = +0x50/+0xA0/+0xF0/+0x140 bytes); the pane text addresses pack +0x28 << 16.

fields.name: textBankId
fields.evidence: Every pane-text setter call packs (u32)self->f_28 << 0x10 | paneId, e.g. icon row i, count row 6+i, total row 0xC.

fields.name: maybe_rowList
fields.evidence: Refresh/SetEntries read self->f_38->f_C as a u16 row/total count and compare it with the number of non-0xFF entries.

fields.name: memberIndex
fields.evidence: Checked against 0x1E and passed to func_0035EB98(work, index) which resolves the party member record; used with SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill(member, skill).

fields.name: skillIds
fields.evidence: Base of the six-entry 0xFF-terminated skill id array (entries at +0x4A..+0x4F); SetEntries copies the incoming ids here and Refresh walks until 0xFF.

fields.name: animRef3Row
fields.evidence: When the entry count is 3, SetEntries calls Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes(self+0x50,1) to switch to the 3-row pane animation.

fields.name: animRef4Row
fields.evidence: When the entry count is 4, Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes(self+0xA0,1) is used.

fields.name: animRef5Row
fields.evidence: When the entry count is 5, Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes(self+0xF0,1) is used.

fields.name: animRef6Row
fields.evidence: When the entry count is 6, Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes(self+0x140,1) is used.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot58
fields.evidence: Artifact: the only evidence is `(**(code**)(*param_1 + 0x58))(param_1)` (vt[+0x58] returns the row list). struct_db multiplied the slot by 4 and emitted offset 0x160; no field exists there (the object is 0x164 bytes).

summary: UI root draw-list object (0x3100 bytes): vtable 0x0076EF80, embedded draw nodes at +0x1C and +0x14C that are spliced into the device primary list, a depth-sorted list node at +0xF8 with depth key (+0x50 base +0x9D bias) and the five-slot sorted draw list at +0x30FC.
evidence: Ui_DrawList_Append 0x0030D404 fills the five 7-word slots of the list at dst+0x8C (each slot = child + 3 position words + 3 depth words); Ui_DrawList_CollectVisible 0x0030DB68 walks 113 child pointers at +0x664 and appends visible ones to self+0x30FC; Ui_DrawList_InsertNodeAt1C/InsertWindowNodes insert the nodes at +0x1C/+0x14C into GfxContext+0x100C; Ui_DrawList_InsertByDepth 0x00547BC4 unlinks/reinserts &self->f_F8 using key (u8 self->f_9D + self->f_50) clamped to 0..0x7F.

fields.name: drawNode
fields.evidence: Ui_DrawList_InsertNodeAt1C (0x00421628) inserts the draw node embedded at self+0x1C into the device's primary UI draw list (GfxContext+0x100C).

fields.name: depthBase
fields.evidence: InsertByDepth computes the sort key as self->f_50 + (u8)self->f_9D before clamping it to 0..0x7F.

fields.name: depthBias
fields.evidence: The byte added to depthBase in InsertByDepth; changing it re-sorts the object in the depth list.

fields.name: depthListNode
fields.evidence: InsertByDepth unlinks &self->f_F8 with func_0011FCBC and re-inserts it with func_0011FCF8 into the depth-sorted list, so +0xF8 is the embedded list node.

fields.name: maybe_listBase
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_DrawList_InsertByDepth2 reads *(int*)(param_1+0x11C) once and uses it as the list owner; role not proven.

fields.name: drawNode2
fields.evidence: Ui_DrawList_InsertWindowNodes (0x00422348) inserts a second node at self+0x14C into the same device draw list.

fields.name: unknown_appendListOffsetArtifact
fields.evidence: Artifact: Ui_DrawList_Append addresses its slot array as dst+0x8C (0x8C bytes = 5 slots of 7 words). struct_db scaled the byte offset by 4 and emitted 0x230; no field exists there.

fields.name: drawList
fields.evidence: Ui_DrawList_CollectVisible calls Ui_DrawList_Append(self+0x30FC); the list occupies 5 slots * 7 words = 0x8C bytes up to the object end 0x3100.

evidence: Ui_SenrekiMonsterList_SetupCamera 0x002435E0 looks up "pCsenreki_monster", "senreki_monster2", "senreki_monster3" with func_0053649C into self->f_50/f_58/f_60, binds "menu_senreki_list_m1"/"m2" with func_001D85E4 at +0xCC, splices list nodes (&self->f_C0, &self->f_7C) and (&self->f_128, &self->f_E4), and writes the view/projection matrix and colour into the GfxContext.

fields.name: monsterPane1

fields.name: monsterPane2
fields.evidence: Result of func_0053649C(monster->f_14, "senreki_monster2") stored at self->f_58.

summary: Skill-panel working buffer (0x464 bytes): a u16 vector of unlockable/pruned skill ids at +0xE (begin/end/capacity words at +0/+4/+8), the current slot byte at +0x30 and the character's 60 learned skill ids at +0x280..+0x460.
evidence: maybe_Ui_SkillList_CollectPruned 0x003AB074 stores the character id in the byte at +3, sets begin = end = self+0xE and capacity = self+0x32, then compacts the surviving skill ids into the u16 vector at +0xE; Ui_SkillList_CollectSorted 0x003AABF0 writes up to 60 sorted ids at +0xE, reads the 60-u16 block from self+0xA0 words (+0x280) to self+0x118 words (+0x460), and stores the slot byte at self[0xC] = +0x30.

fields.name: skillIdBegin
fields.evidence: CollectPruned writes *self = self+0xE (start of the inline u16 vector) and the vector is compacted between begin/end at +0/+4.

fields.name: skillIdEnd
fields.evidence: CollectPruned sets self[1] = self+0xE and advances it as ids are appended (`local_30[1] = puVar15 + 1`).

fields.name: skillIdCapacityEnd
fields.evidence: CollectPruned sets self[2] = self+0x32 (capacity end of the pruned vector) and checks it before growing.

fields.name: skillIdBuffer
fields.evidence: Inline u16 storage: CollectSorted writes the sorted ids as *(u16*)(self + i*2 + 0xE); the begin pointer is self+0xE.

fields.name: slot
fields.evidence: CollectSorted writes (char)slot to self[0xC] = +0x30; CollectPruned takes the same slot as its third argument.

fields.name: unknown_capacityValueArtifact
fields.evidence: Artifact: the only evidence is the value `(int)self + 0x32` stored into +8 (capacity end). struct_db emitted the value as a field offset; there is no independent access at +0x32.

fields.name: learnedSkillIds
fields.evidence: CollectSorted walks the 60-entry u16 array starting at self+0xA0 words = +0x280 (`puVar9 = (u16*)(self+0xA0)`) when checking prerequisites.

fields.name: learnedSkillIdsEnd
fields.evidence: End sentinel of the 60-entry array: CollectSorted stops at self+0x118 words = +0x460.

summary: bflyt animation-track list (0x1C bytes): vtable 0x007813A4, an allocator/count pair at +4/+8, a self-linked intrusive list at +0x10/+0x14 whose nodes wrap one animation track each, and the source record table at +0x18.
evidence: Ui_AnimTrackList_CtorFromRecords 0x00538DB0 installs 0x007813A4, zeroes +4/+8/+C, sets +0x10 and +0x14 to &self[4 words]=+0x10 (empty list sentinel), stores table+8 at +0x18 and appends one 0x0C-byte wrapper per 0x18-byte track record (table->f_2A count) through owner vt[+0x2C]; the caller is the confident Ui_Layout_LoadBflyt.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor stores the literal 0x007813A4 at +0.

fields.name: maybe_allocator
fields.evidence: Zeroed here; the sibling notification list (Ui_NotifyList) copies the owner heap into this word and uses it as the allocation heap, so it is probably the same list-base allocator field.

fields.name: maybe_listSize
fields.evidence: Zeroed by the ctor; no reader in this batch, so only a list-size candidate.

fields.name: maybe_listLinkBase
fields.evidence: Passed as the first argument of func_0011FCF8(self+3 words, self+4 words, node) when each track wrapper is inserted.

fields.name: maybe_listNext
fields.evidence: Set to the self-referential sentinel &self[4 words] = +0x10 by the ctor; second argument of the insert helper.

fields.name: maybe_listPrev
fields.evidence: Set to the same sentinel +0x10 by the ctor (`self[5] = self+4`), i.e. the previous link of the empty ring.

fields.name: recordTable
fields.evidence: Ctor stores table+8 here; the 0x18-byte animation track records are read from table+0x2C and counted by table->f_2A.

summary: Notification-list object (0x1C bytes) built per UI context and registered at (work+8)->f_7C+0x1C: vtable 0x00782234, allocation heap at +4, an intrusive notification list at +8..+0x10, a constant sort helper at +0x14 and the owner back-pointer at +0x18.
evidence: Ui_NotifyList_Ctor 0x003F2EFC installs 0x00782234, copies owner->f_4 into +4, self-links +8/+0xC/+0x10 to &self[2 words]=+8, stores the constant 0x007807E0 at +0x14 and self at +0x18, drains the list, calls maybe_Ui_NotifyList_BuildEntries (0x003F2AF4) and registers the object at (work+8)->f_7C+0x1C; Ui_NotifyList_Dtor 0x003F2FA8 clears that registration and re-links the sentinels.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor and Dtor install the literal 0x00782234 at +0.

fields.name: allocator
fields.evidence: Ctor copies *(u32*)(owner+4) here; BuildEntries passes *(u32*)(self+4) to Mem_AllocAligned_2 for every new 0x14-byte node.

fields.name: maybe_listNext
fields.evidence: First word of the self-referential list sentinel: `self[2] = self+2 words` (+8); BuildEntries inserts at self+8 and sorts self+8.

fields.name: maybe_listPrev
fields.evidence: Second sentinel word (`self[3] = self+2 words`), used as the sort comparator/end argument of std_List_MergeSort.

fields.name: maybe_listEnd
fields.evidence: Third sentinel word (`self[4] = self+2 words`), reset by the destructor together with +8/+0xC.

fields.name: maybe_comparator
fields.evidence: The ctor stores the constant 0x007807E0 here; the sibling lists use a sort helper in the matching slot between the sentinel and the owner pointer.

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: Ctor stores self here (`self[6] = self`) and the destructor walks/relinks the list using it as the back-pointer.
